t: Sigismund dethroned in Sweden
c: Sigismund's ultra-Catholicism appeared threatening to the Swedish Protestant establishment and contributed to his dethronement in Sweden in 1599.

t: Sigismund humiliated at sejm
c: Accused by Zamoyski of breaking his covenants, Sigismund III was humiliated during the sejm of 1592, which deepened his resentment of szlachta.

t: Battle of Guzów ends Polish civil war
c: The ensuing civil war was resolved at the Battle of Guzów, where the szlachta was defeated in 1607.

t: John Sigismund inherits Duchy of Prussia

t: Uniate Church eliminated in Dnieper region
c: Cossacks felt being members of the "Rus' Orthodox nation" (the Uniate Church was practically eliminated in the Dnieper region in 1633).

t: Nalyvaiko Uprising engulfs Ukraine and Belarus
c: New fighting took place already in 1594, when the Nalyvaiko Uprising engulfed large portions of Ukraine and Belarus.

t: Żółkiewski defeats Cossacks; Nalyvaiko executed
c: Hetman Stanisław Żółkiewski defeated the Cossack units in 1596 and Severyn Nalyvaiko was executed.

t: Marek Zhmaylo uprising suppressed
c: The uprising of Marek Zhmaylo of 1625 was confronted by Stanisław Koniecpolski and concluded with Mykhailo Doroshenko signing the Treaty of Kurukove.

t: Pavluk Uprising begins
c: Another round of fighting, the Pavluk Uprising, followed in 1637–1638.

t: Death of Władysław's son Zygmunt Kazimierz
c: Władysław's son Zygmunt Kazimierz died in 1647, and the King, weakened, resigned and disappointed, in 1648.

c: Turkey, threatened by the Polish territorial gains became involved at the frontiers, and a peace between Russia and Sweden was agreed to in 1617.

t: Koniecpolski defeats Tugay Bey at Okhmativ
c: In 1644 Koniecpolski defeated Tugay Bey's army at Okhmativ and before his death planned an invasion against the Crimean Khanate.

t: Sejm thwarts king's Ottoman crusade plans
c: King Władysław IV's ideas of a grand international war-crusade against the Ottoman Empire were thwarted by the inquisition sejm in 1646.

t: Bogislaw XIV, Duke of Pomerania, dies
c: In 1637 Bogislaw XIV, Duke of Pomerania died.

t: Polish peasantry rebellion in Silesia
c: In Silesia the ethnically Polish peasantry rebelled during 1722–29 and in 1750 around Pszczyna, when the Prussian army was brought to bear.

t: French Huguenots establish trading house in Warsaw
c: A major trading house was established in Warsaw by French Huguenots in 1723.

t: Smolensk falls to Russian siege
c: Belarusian towns surrendered one after another and in 1654 Smolensk fell after a three-month-long siege.

t: Truce of Vilnius accord signed
c: With the simultaneous Swedish war disasters the Commonwealth had to accede in 1656 to the Truce of Vilnius accord.

t: Polish-Brandenburg-Austrian expedition launched
c: In 1658 a joint Polish-Brandenburg-Austrian expedition into Swedish Pomerania and then Denmark took place.

t: John Sobieski confronts Tatar-Cossack forces at Lwów
c: In 1667, when Tatar-Cossack forces attacked Lwów (Lviv), Hetman John Sobieski confronted them with a small force.

t: John III Sobieski elected king; continues war with Turkey
c: John Sobieski, elected in 1674 as King John III, continued the war with Turkey.

t: Lubomirski leads Polish military expedition into Hungary
c: The Hungarian rebels were helped with volunteers and supply, and in 1677 with a military expedition led into Hungary by Hieronim Lubomirski.

t: Ottoman Sultan Mehmed IV prepares against Austria
c: Mehmed IV, having concluded in 1681 the war with Russia, was getting ready to take up the defense of Thököly and move against Austria.

t: Treaty of Karlowitz concluded
c: The final Treaty of Karlowitz concluded in 1699 the Holy League's wars with the Ottoman Empire.

c: Augustus' expeditions into Western Pomerania in 1711–13 with the Danes and Russians resulted only in the Prussian takeover of Stettin.

t: Frederick Augustus converts and marries Maria Josepha
c: Son Frederick Augustus converted to Catholicism and in 1719 married Maria Josepha, daughter of Emperor Joseph I.

t: Frederick invades Silesia
c: Taking advantage of the Habsburg dynastic crisis after the assumption of the throne by Maria Theresa, he invaded Silesia in 1740.

t: Treaties of Breslau and Berlin cede Silesia
c: The Treaty of Breslau and Treaty of Berlin (1742) gave Prussia the majority of the Silesian territory.

t: Saxon army destroyed in Olomouc campaign
c: The Saxon army, allied with Prussia, was destroyed during Frederick's Olomouc campaign in 1742.

t: Treaty of Hubertusburg preserves territorial status quo
c: Despite the far reaching Prussian and Russian expansionist designs, the Treaty of Hubertusburg preserved the territorial status quo in the area in 1763.

t: Protestants forbidden to restore congregations
c: In 1717, after the Northern War destruction, Protestants were not allowed to restore the structures of their congregations or build new ones.

t: Jesuit Breslau Academy established
c: The Jesuit Breslau Academy was established in 1702 and attracted students form the Commonwealth.

t: Nowe Ateny encyclopedia published
c: Nowe Ateny (The New Athens), the first encyclopedia published by Benedykt Chmielowski in 1745–46, was not scientifically current.

t: Kurier Polski newspaper begins publication
c: The first permanent newspaper was Kurier Polski, published from 1729 by the Piarists and then the Jesuits.

t: Collegium Nobilium established in Warsaw
c: In 1740 he established the Collegium Nobilium in Warsaw, a high caliber secondary education institution for nobility youth.

t: Piarist colleges reformed
c: In 1754 all the Piarist colleges were reformed and the Jesuit schools soon followed.

t: Załuski Library opened to public
c: In 1747 they opened a public library in Warsaw, known as the Załuski Library, one of the largest in Europe.

t: Commission of National Education established in Poland
c: In 1773 the Sejm established the Commission of National Education, a pioneering in Europe government education authority.

t: Royal Castle and Łazienki Palace rebuilt
c: The King had the interior of the Royal Castle redone and after 1783 the summer Łazienki Palace rebuilt in the style of classicism by Domenico Merlini.

t: Stanisław August Poniatowski crowned in Warsaw
c: The coronation and the Coronation Sejm took place in 1764, for the first (and last) time in Warsaw.

t: Repnin demands restoration of religious minority rights
c: At the sejm of 1767 Repnin demanded that the rights of religious minorities be restored.
